Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The study is a metaproteomics analysis of faecal samples. While the protocol uses 'protein aggregation capture' via magnetic beads to concentrate proteins from the slurry, this is a general sample preparation/cleanup step for the total protein extract from the faeces, not a specific affinity-purification of a target protein or complex. Therefore, it is classified as whole cell lysate (metaproteome). Mixed species flag is true as both human and bacterial proteins were analyzed.

primary_biological_variables.matched_definition: Comparison between diseased and healthy or unaffected controls.
evidence: We study the changes in the microbiome of children diagnosed with CMA some of whom outgrew their CMA after one year and others did not.
Analysis of metaproteomics data was done by grouping the subjects into those that outgrew their CMA or those that did not at visit 12 months.
Some infants received an amino acid-based formula (AAF)
others received an AAF with a synbiotic blend (AAF-syn) (oligosaccharides (oligofructose, inulin) + Bifidobacterium breve M-16 V)
Faecal microbiota composition of infants was analysed directly after CMA diagnosis (baseline) as well as 6 and 12 months after entering the study.
For those 40 infants, samples were collected at three visits, resulting in 120 samples
To indicate which samples belong to the same subject in the pairwise comparisons between visits, a subject variable was included in the analysis.
compare infants who outgrew their CMA with infants that did not
significantly higher relative abundances of Ruminococcaceae at visit 12 months compared to baseline visit in the group with outgrowth of CMA

The differential analysis is complex, utilizing Linear Mixed Models (LMM) to account for longitudinal sampling (baseline, 6m, 12m) and subject-level random effects.
